## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing list-based respawn into a compiler-auto-vectorized per-particle update loop can sustain near-streaming-ceiling bandwidth even under moderate death churn.

## Cache saturation
All measured N values exceed the L1d spill (N≈897), so every data point already resides beyond L1. The L2 spill at N≈57456 falls between N=10000 and N=100000. At q=0.01, cost actually falls across that boundary — from 9.075 ns/p at N=10000 to 8.359 at N=100000 — reflecting overhead amortization rather than any spill knee. Beyond N=100000 the curve is flat: 8.359, 8.473, 8.415 at N=10⁵, 10⁶, 10⁷. Raising the death rate lifts the floor without reshaping the N-curve: q=0.1 holds at ~10.3–11.2 ns/p, q=0.25 at ~13.3, and q=0.5 at ~18.0–18.3, all essentially flat across N. No cache-spill knee appears at either transition; the algo is not DRAM-bandwidth-limited at any measured scale.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 8.73 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — only 29% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is compute-bound at low churn: the q=0.01 profile shows 64–71% compute cycles. Bandwidth erodes monotonically with death rate: 8.73 → 7.1 → 5.48 → 4.0 GB/s as q rises from 0.01 to 0.5, tracking the branch-flush share which climbs from 5% to 41%. The transition from compute-bound to branch-bound occurs around q=0.1, where branch_flush reaches 23% and compute drops below 61%. The algo never approaches the streaming ceiling in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of a single particle, not across particles. The loop advances by stride 0x44 (68 bytes) per iteration, loading a 128-bit block via `ldur q16` and applying `fmul.4s` / `fadd.4s` on four floats, then `fmul.2s` / `fadd.2s` on the next pair. An `ext.16b` rearranges lanes and `mov.s v18[3], v7[0]` inserts a computed scalar. A gather appears as `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x11]`, loading one float into a single lane from a non-contiguous offset. Mask writes are byte-granular (`strb w10, [x24, x8]`), and the respawn path issues `bl` calls to `_layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn` and `_layouts.common.render_simple.splat`. This component-wise vec on stride-68 data explains the sub-ceiling bandwidth: the per-particle SIMD is narrow, and the byte stores plus branchy respawn path prevent streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo peaks at 8.73 GB/s = 29% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling at q=0.01, N=100000, and collapses to 4.0 GB/s (13%) at q=0.5 where branch_flush reaches 41%. Component-wise auto-vectorization within a single 68-byte particle cannot approach streaming bandwidth, and the fused list-respawn path's branchiness dominates as death rate rises, confirming the hypothesis fails in every measured regime.
